assumptions.condition: Every \(G_S\) represents the unrestricted semi-Markovian SCM class associated with that ADMG.
\(\mathcal T\) is a nice tree decomposition of \(\operatorname{Inc}(\mathcal O_{XY})\) of width \(\tau\).

definitions.name: Minimal failure-support hypergraph
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal O_{XY}=\{S\subseteq E^{?}:\operatorname{Fail}(S)=1\text{ and }\operatorname{Fail}(S\setminus\{e\})=0\text{ for every }e\in S\}\).

definitions.name: Sparse hedge-core family
definitions.construction: Enumerate tuples \(c=(F_0,F_1,A,K_c)\) inside one bidirected district of \(G^{+}\), where \(\varnothing\ne A\subseteq F_0\subsetneq F_1\), \(F_0\cap X=\varnothing\), and \(F_1\cap X\ne\varnothing\). Select one outgoing directed edge toward \(A\) for every vertex of \(F_1\setminus A\), with the selections on \(F_0\setminus A\) retained inside the larger forest; select a bidirected spanning tree of \(F_0\) and extend it to a bidirected spanning tree of \(F_1\). Let \(K_c\) be the uncertain edges in this common selected union, and retain only tuples whose selected edges occur in \(G^{+}\).

definitions.name: Root-ordered sparse-core extendability handle
definitions.construction: Start from each \(c\in\mathfrak C\); project maximal deterministic directed reachability outside \(X\); order the roots in \(A_c\); branch only on uncertain edges assigned to the first root whose current reachability obligation they privately satisfy; query whether a partial support extends to a support not dominated by a completed support from any core; and recompute the canonical ID failure label only when a support is emitted.

definitions.name: Obstruction independence polynomial
definitions.construction: \(I_{\mathcal O}(\lambda)=\sum_{J\subseteq E^{?}:\,\forall h\in\mathcal O_{XY},\,h\nsubseteq J}\prod_{e\in J}\lambda_e\).

definitions.name: Available labelled bows
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal B=\{\beta=(x,r,e^{\to},e^{\leftrightarrow}):x\in X,\ r\in V\setminus X,\ e^{\to}=(x\to r)\in E^{\mathrm{det}}\cup E^{?},\ e^{\leftrightarrow}=(x\leftrightarrow r)\in E^{\mathrm{det}}\cup E^{?}\}\); write \(r_\beta=r\).

definitions.name: Width-two transition vertices
definitions.construction: Let \(E^{?}_{\to,\bar X}=\{e\in E^{?}:e\text{ is directed and }\operatorname{tail}(e),\operatorname{head}(e)\in V\setminus X\}\). Set \(W^{\mathrm{proj}}=\{\sigma,t\}\cup\{u_\beta:\beta\in\mathcal B\}\cup\{u_e:e\in E^{?}_{\to,\bar X}\}\), where \(\sigma\) is the super-source and \(t\) is the sink.

definitions.name: Width-two uncertain-edge labels
definitions.construction: Define \(L:W^{\mathrm{proj}}\to2^{E^{?}}\) by \(L(\sigma)=L(t)=\varnothing\), \(L(u_\beta)=\{e^{\to},e^{\leftrightarrow}\}\cap E^{?}\) for \(\beta=(x,r,e^{\to},e^{\leftrightarrow})\), and \(L(u_e)=\{e\}\). For a directed path \(P\), set \(L(P)=\bigcup_{u\in P}L(u)\).

definitions.name: Width-two transition arcs
definitions.construction: Let \(D=(V\setminus X,E^{\mathrm{det}}_{\to}[V\setminus X])\), and let \(a\leadsto_D B\) mean that \(D\) has a possibly length-zero directed path from \(a\) to a vertex of \(B\). The arc set \(A^{\mathrm{proj}}\) contains exactly: \(\sigma\to u_\beta\) for every \(\beta\in\mathcal B\); \(u_\beta\to t\) when \(r_\beta\leadsto_D Y\); \(u_\beta\to u_e\) when \(r_\beta\leadsto_D\{\operatorname{tail}(e)\}\); \(u_e\to t\) when \(\operatorname{head}(e)\leadsto_D Y\); and \(u_e\to u_f\) when \(\operatorname{head}(e)\leadsto_D\{\operatorname{tail}(f)\}\).

definitions.name: Width-two deterministic-path projection
definitions.construction: For \(b\le2\), set \(T^{\mathrm{proj}}=(W^{\mathrm{proj}},A^{\mathrm{proj}})\) with vertex set, uncertain-edge labels, and arcs from Definitions~\ref{def:transition-vertices}--\ref{def:transition-arcs}. Order bow vertices and uncertain-edge vertices by their endpoint tuples under \(\prec\), and initialize the prefixes \((\sigma,u_\beta)\) in that order. For a chordless prefix \(P=(\sigma,u_1,\ldots,u_k)\), form \(H(P)\) by deleting every unused vertex \(w\) with \(u_i\to w\in A^{\mathrm{proj}}\) for some \(i<k\); its children append, in \(\prec\)-order, each out-neighbor \(w\) of \(u_k\) in \(H(P)\) from which \(t\) is reachable in \(H(P)\). At \(t\), let \(U=L(P)\); emit \(U\) exactly when, for every \(e\in U\), the subgraph induced by \(\{u:L(u)\subseteq U\setminus\{e\}\}\) has no \(\sigma\)-to-\(t\) path, and when \(P\) is the \(\prec\)-least chordless path with label union \(U\), found by the same ordered reachability rule.

definitions.name: Deterministic-diamond worked instance
definitions.construction: Let \(\mathcal D\) have ordered vertices \(x\prec r\prec a\prec b\prec c\prec y\), intervention \(X=\{x\}\), outcome \(Y=\{y\}\), deterministic directed edges \(r\to a,r\to b,a\to c,b\to c,c\to y\), uncertain edges \(e_1=x\to r\) and \(e_2=x\leftrightarrow r\), and query \(P_x(y)\).

statements.statement: For all \(S,T\subseteq E^{?}\), if \(S\subseteq T\) and \(\operatorname{Fail}(S)=1\), then \(\operatorname{Fail}(T)=1\).
statements.justification: Upward closure turns causal failure into a monotone Boolean property whose prime supports are exactly \(\mathcal O_{XY}\).
statements.gap: Akbari et al. (2023, Lemma 3) prove the contrapositive formula-validity statement; this lemma records the exact support order used by the compiler.
statements.consumer: It permits single-edge deletion tests for global minimality and the obstruction-free reliability formula.

statements.statement: Every \(h\in\mathcal O_{XY}\) is a globally inclusion-minimal member of \(\bigcup_{c\in\mathfrak C}\{K_c\cup J:\text{ every }a\in A_c\text{ reaches }Y\text{ in the directed part of }(V,E^{\mathrm{det}}\cup K_c\cup J)[V\setminus X]\}\), and every globally minimal member of this union belongs to \(\mathcal O_{XY}\). Each \(K_c\) contains at most \(2b-2\) selected edges, and \(|\mathfrak C|\le |V|2^{O(b\log(b+1))}\).
statements.justification: The theorem isolates all unbounded support size in directed ancestry while keeping the genuinely causal hedge templates fixed-parameter bounded.
statements.gap: Shpitser (2023, Proposition 1) gives the original-query hedge equivalence, and Akbari et al. provide a hedge hull, but neither gives a sparse edge-labelled template representation across uncertain realizations.
statements.consumer: It reduces causal obstruction compilation to a bounded-root directed support problem usable by the general enumerator.

statements.statement: Can the root-ordered sparse-core extendability handle be realized by a finite partial-support state and child map such that every live child has a globally minimal completion, children partition all completions, completed supports are never dominated by another core, and the extension test runs in \(2^{O(b\log b)}\operatorname{poly}(|V|+|E^{\mathrm{det}}|+|E^{?}|)\) time?
statements.justification: This is the genuine open step: completed-support dominators are ordered, but their obligations have not been shown stable under partial extension across competing cores.
statements.gap: Steiner branching supplies extension for fully selectable edge witnesses, and bounded-treewidth transversal branching supplies extension for an explicit hypergraph; neither provides this projected, implicit, cross-core extension oracle.
statements.consumer: A positive resolution supplies the missing correctness and worst-delay invariant for the obstruction compiler; a negative resolution identifies the parameter that must replace \(b\).

statements.statement: There is a deterministic algorithm that, after \(2^{O(b\log b)}\operatorname{poly}(|V|+|E^{\mathrm{det}}|+|E^{?}|)\) preprocessing, enumerates every member of \(\mathcal O_{XY}\) exactly once with the same worst-case delay and polynomial working space; its first output and exhaustion obey the same bound, every output is globally minimal, and each output receives a canonical original-query ID failure label.
statements.justification: This is the theorem-level kernel converting one uncertain causal graph into a complete, auditable antichain of failure explanations.
statements.gap: The nearest causal algorithms return one optimal edge deletion or discover only the hedges needed for an intervention optimum; no cited result proves output-sensitive uncertain-edge support enumeration.
statements.consumer: The uncertain-ADMG sampler and edgeID workflow can report every minimal jointly harmful edge combination rather than one selected identifiable realization.

statements.statement: If \(b\le2\), then \(\operatorname{Fail}(S)=1\) if and only if there is \(\beta=(x,r,e^{\to},e^{\leftrightarrow})\in\mathcal B\) whose two edges lie in \(E^{\mathrm{det}}\cup S\) and for which \(r\) reaches \(Y\) in the directed part of \(G_S[V\setminus X]\). Moreover, \(\mathcal O_{XY}\) is exactly the family of inclusion-minimal label unions \(L(P)\) of \(\sigma\)-to-\(t\) paths in \(T^{\mathrm{proj}}\). The child rule in Definition~\ref{def:width-two-projection}, retaining only the \(\prec\)-least chordless representative of each label union and testing label-union minimality by reachability, enumerates every member exactly once with polynomial preprocessing, worst-case delay, exhaustion time, and space. For a fixed label union, the ordered singleton-labelled internal vertices are unique and at most \(|\mathcal B|\) bow vertices can supply candidate representatives.
statements.justification: Shpitser (2023, Proposition 1) supplies the original-query hedge equivalence; the theorem specializes its certificates at district size two and validates a complete projection algorithm without the unresolved multiple-root recursion.
statements.gap: The original-query criterion in Shpitser (2023, Proposition 1) is not an enumeration result, while directed-path and Steiner enumeration do not suppress the exponential multiplicity of deterministic path witnesses or collisions between bow starts that yield the same uncertain support.
statements.consumer: It gives an immediately implementable exact compiler for uncertain envelopes with only pairwise latent-confounding districts.

statements.statement: For \(\mathcal D\), the largest bidirected district has size \(b=2\), the two distinct deterministic directed paths \(r\to a\to c\to y\) and \(r\to b\to c\to y\) induce the same single transition arc \(u_\beta\to t\), and the unique minimal failure support is \(\{e_1,e_2\}\). Hence the projected enumerator emits \(\{e_1,e_2\}\) once, independently of the number of deterministic paths represented by that transition arc.
statements.justification: The instance exposes the exact duplicate mechanism that deterministic-path projection must quotient before enumeration.
statements.gap: Ordinary path enumeration visits both arms of the deterministic diamond even though neither arm changes the uncertain-edge support.
statements.consumer: It is a worked regression test for projection, label-union canonicalization, and duplicate suppression in the width-two compiler.

statements.statement: On the full real cube \(p\in[0,1]^{E^{?}}\), \(R_{XY}(p)=\sum_{S\subseteq E^{?}:\operatorname{Fail}(S)=0}\prod_{e\in S}p_e\prod_{e\in E^{?}\setminus S}(1-p_e)\) is a multilinear polynomial and \(\partial R_{XY}/\partial p_e=-\Pr_{p_{-e}}\{\operatorname{Fail}(Z\setminus\{e\})=0,\operatorname{Fail}(Z\cup\{e\})=1\}\in[-1,0]\), including at boundary points by polynomial evaluation. On the interior cube \(p\in(0,1)^{E^{?}}\), the same polynomial satisfies \(R_{XY}(p)=\prod_{e\in E^{?}}(1-p_e)\,I_{\mathcal O}((p_e/(1-p_e))_{e\in E^{?}})\).
statements.justification: This is an algebraic implementation corollary of compiling the monotone failure event into its minimal-support antichain, not an independent novelty claim.
statements.gap: Akbari et al. use products of edge probabilities to rank one realization; after the new obstruction compiler makes the negative monotone clauses explicit, the total mass and pivotal-edge derivative identities follow by standard literal weighting and conditioning.
statements.consumer: Practitioners obtain total confidence and the marginal value of resolving uncertainty about each edge from the compiler output.

statements.statement: As an implementation corollary of Proposition~\ref{prop:reliability-implementation-corollary} and standard exact literal-weighted CNF model counting on incidence decompositions, given \(\mathcal O_{XY}\), an exact-arithmetic input \(p\in(\mathbb Q\cap[0,1])^{E^{?}}\), and \(\mathcal T\), one can compute \(R_{XY}(p)\) and every coordinate of \(\nabla R_{XY}(p)\) exactly in \(2^{O(\tau)}\operatorname{poly}(|\mathcal O_{XY}|+|E^{?}|+|\mathcal T|+B)\) bit operations, where \(B\) is the total input bit length of \(p\). A standard project--join bag state records assignments of incident uncertain-edge vertices and one witnessed-zero flag for each obstruction clause; derivatives use the conditioned evaluations \(p_e=1\) and \(p_e=0\), so the guarantee includes boundary coordinates.
statements.justification: The proposition records a standard exact weighted-model-counting implementation of the newly compiled obstruction hypergraph and charges the supplied decomposition and rational bit lengths.
statements.gap: Samer and Szeider supply the incidence-treewidth counting recurrence, and Dudek et al. supply literal-weighted project--join dynamic programming; this proposition claims no new generic dynamic program and only instantiates those methods after causal obstruction compilation.
statements.consumer: edgeID can evaluate identification reliability and graph-refinement sensitivities whenever the emitted support hypergraph has small incidence treewidth.

statements.statement: Computing \(N_{XY}\) is \(\#\mathrm{P}\)-complete under polynomial-time counting reductions even for topologically ordered envelopes with \(b=2\). Hardness holds when every uncertain edge has probability \(1/2\): prepend to an acyclic source--sink network the deterministic edges \(x\to s\) and \(x\leftrightarrow s\), query \(P_x(t)\), and invoke Shpitser (2023, Proposition 1) to obtain equivalence between original-query ID failure and \(s\)-to-\(t\) reachability; membership follows by guessing \(S\) and running ordinary ID.
statements.justification: The lower bound shows that small causal districts permit output-sensitive explanations without making the total probability problem easy.
statements.gap: Akbari et al. establish NP-completeness of selecting one identifiable graph; Provan establishes reliability counting hardness without a causal width-preserving reduction.
statements.consumer: The result tells users when exact reliability needs structural width such as \(\tau\), despite a simple latent-confounding pattern.

statements.statement: For every \(k\ge1\), there is an envelope with \(b=2\), \(O(k)\) vertices and edges, and \(|\mathcal O_{XY}|=2^k\). There is also a family with \(b=2\) and polynomial-size \(\mathcal O_{XY}\) whose incidence treewidth is unbounded.
statements.justification: The two constructions separate causal district width, output size, and reliability-evaluation width.
statements.gap: Neither causal identification nor classical reliability work records this three-way parameter separation for uncertain ADMG queries.
statements.consumer: It prevents misleading total-time claims and guides whether users should enumerate, compile by incidence width, or approximate.

statements.statement: For the graph with deterministic \(X\to M\to Y\), uncertain \(X\to Y\) of probability \(q\in[0,1]\), and uncertain \(X\leftrightarrow Y\) of probability \(r\in[0,1]\), \(\mathcal O_{XY}=\{\{X\to Y,X\leftrightarrow Y\}\}\), \(R_{XY}=1-qr\), \(\partial R_{XY}/\partial q=-r\), and \(\partial R_{XY}/\partial r=-q\), including on the boundary of the square.
statements.justification: This reduction recovers the familiar bow obstruction and checks the sign and normalization of the reliability gradient.
statements.gap: It is a required special-case reduction, not an independent novelty claim.
statements.consumer: It supplies a transparent unit test for any implementation of enumeration and exact differentiation.

sampling_model.design: Independent Bernoulli realization of uncertain directed and bidirected edges in a fixed topologically ordered ADMG envelope.
sampling_model.units: The finite vertices \(V\) are fixed; there is no sampling of observational units in the theorem.
sampling_model.treatment: The intervention set \(X\) and outcome set \(Y\) are fixed before the edge realization.
sampling_model.overlap: Not applicable; the real probabilities \(p_e\in[0,1]\) encode structural uncertainty rather than treatment assignment.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None; \(p\in[0,1]^{E^{?}}\) and the envelope are computational inputs. Rational coordinates are required only when the exact bit-complexity guarantee is invoked, and no calibration claim for estimated edge probabilities is made.
sampling_model.randomness: Only \(Z\) is random, with mutually independent coordinates.

estimand_functional: \(R_{XY}(p)=\Pr_p\{P_x(y)\text{ is identifiable in }G_Z\}=\sum_{S:\operatorname{Fail}(S)=0}\prod_{e\in S}p_e\prod_{e\notin S}(1-p_e),\quad p\in[0,1]^{E^{?}}\)

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The edge ID problem is NP-complete.
Lemma 7 states that Algorithm 2 returns an optimal solution to the minimum-cost intervention problem in Equation (2).
We can enumerate all minimal directed Steiner trees in \(O(nm)\) delay and \(O(n+m)\) space.
The minimal transversals can be enumerated in fixed-parameter-linear delay following an FPT preprocessing phase.
Our algorithm runs in time \(O(4^k k\ell N)\).
Source--sink reliability is \(\#\mathrm{P}\)-complete even for acyclic directed planar graphs having vertex degree at most three.
The ID algorithm is complete for identification of interventional distributions in semi-Markovian causal models.
Proposition 1 states that the ID algorithm fails exactly when a hedge exists for the original identification query.
The directed path-conjunction special case admits polynomial-delay enumeration.
Project--join trees support exact weighted model counting by dynamic programming.
Network reliability is fixed-parameter tractable for bounded-treewidth networks.
Counting vertex covers in bipartite graphs is \(\#\mathrm{P}\)-complete.

tldr: A probabilistic ADMG currently yields one high-plausibility identifiable realization, not the total chance that a fixed causal query is identifiable or the minimal edge combinations that destroy it. The proposal makes those combinations the hyperedges of \(\mathcal O_{XY}\), compresses every hedge into a \(2b-2\)-edge core plus directed ancestry obligations, and targets a canonical \(2^{O(b\log b)}\)-delay compiler. The full \(b\le2\) class is handled by a formally labelled transition DAG; a deterministic-diamond instance shows that distinct deterministic paths yield one uncertain-edge support and one output. Once the new compiler makes \(\mathcal O_{XY}\) explicit, standard exact literal-weighted CNF model counting on an incidence decomposition yields reliability and all edge sensitivities as an implementation corollary, while a width-two causal reduction proves that exact successful-realization counting remains \(\#\mathrm{P}\)-complete.

project_justification.gap: Ordinary ID certifies failure in one ADMG by a hedge, and edgeID chooses one plausible identifiable subgraph, but neither theory enumerates the globally minimal uncertain-edge causes of failure across all realizations.
project_justification.niche: Maximum envelope district size bounds the local bidirected and forest part of every hedge without bounding its directed ancestry paths. This exposes a parameterized enumeration problem that is causal in its core and combinatorial in its unbounded remainder.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies a sparse-core representation, a canonical duplicate-free compiler with a complete width-two construction, a standard weighted-model-counting implementation corollary for the compiled output, and a sharp width-two causal counting-complexity boundary.

related_work: Shpitser and Pearl (2008) establish soundness and completeness of ordinary ID through hedge certificates; Shpitser (2023, Proposition 1, \(\mathrm{arXiv}:2307.03750\)) gives the corrected equivalence between ID failure and a hedge for the original query. These results supply the causal equivalence used here, not support-enumeration results. Akbari et al. (2023) formulate probabilistic ADMGs and prove edge ID is NP-complete, but their objective selects one edge-deleted identifiable graph. In the final JMLR article, Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash (2025, Definition 6 and Algorithm 2 on pages 10--12, with optimality in Lemma 7) define vertex-minimal hedges, iteratively discover only enough such hedges to solve a minimum hitting-set intervention problem, and explicitly avoid enumerating all hedges. That machinery optimizes interventions in one fixed graph; it neither enumerates uncertain-edge-minimal supports for failure of the original query nor proves output-sensitive delay under deterministic-path projection and cross-core domination. Khachiyan et al. (2007) and Kobayashi, Kurita, and Wasa (2022) provide path and directed-Steiner enumeration techniques, but their selected-edge witnesses do not identify deterministic paths that collapse to the same uncertain support. Kenig and Mizrahi (2025) obtain fixed-parameter-linear delay for minimal transversals when an explicit incidence decomposition is supplied, whereas this project must first compile an implicit causal obstruction hypergraph under parameter \(b\). Samer and Szeider (2010) supply standard exact CNF model counting at bounded incidence treewidth, and Dudek, Phan, and Vardi (2020) supply standard literal-weighted project--join dynamic programming. The reliability and full-gradient computations here are an implementation consequence of those generic methods after the new causal compiler emits \(\mathcal O_{XY}\), not an independently novel dynamic program. Goharshady and Mohammadi (2020) compute classical network reliability at bounded network treewidth and further confirm that the counting component belongs to established reliability methodology. Provan (1986) and Provan and Ball (1983) supply the counting-hardness sources for the width-preserving causal reduction.
technical_internal_limitation: A completed minimal ancestry support gives each uncertain edge a private root and orders that root's mandatory edges as dominators, but the private-root assignment has not been proved stable for partial supports. Distinct cores may yield the same completion or a strict superset of another completion. The general delay theorem therefore cannot be obtained by enumerating path witnesses and filtering: deterministic diamonds create exponentially many witnesses for one uncertain support, and post-output filtering does not bound exhaustion delay.
honest_scope: The sparse-core reduction, the complete \(b\le2\) labelled-transition-DAG algorithm, and the width-two counting reduction are theorem targets, not established results. The reliability identity, full-gradient formula, and incidence-treewidth computation are explicitly implementation propositions obtained from the compiled obstruction hypergraph by standard exact literal-weighted CNF model counting and project--join dynamic programming; they are not claimed as an independent algorithmic novelty. The deterministic-diamond proposition is a worked projection and duplicate-suppression check, not a substitute for the general width-two proof. The root-ordered partial-support recursion for general \(b\) is the open kernel. Its first kill test is exhaustive comparison with brute-force minimal supports on all specified envelopes with at most six vertices, \(b\le3\), and at most eight uncertain edges; any missing support, duplicate, false live branch, or loss of global minimality rejects the state design. No claim is made that the edge probabilities are calibrated, that one identifying formula is common to all successful realizations, or that \(b\) controls total output size.

seed_details.proposal: Enumerate every inclusion-minimal uncertain-edge support for failure of ordinary identification with \(2^{O(b\log b)}\) polynomial preprocessing and worst-case delay by sparse hedge cores and a canonical multiple-root ancestry recursion.
seed_details.anchor_receipt: Read the Introduction, Lemma 3, the edge ID definition, Lemma 4, Theorem 1 and its reduction proof, and the concluding remarks in the arXiv source. The paper optimizes one edge-deleted identifiable graph; the first unresolved proof step for enumeration is replacing optimization stopping with a partition of all globally minimal failure supports.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The edge ID reduction supplies a feasibility oracle but not an extendability oracle for partial uncertain-edge supports; the first new step is a canonical child partition after deterministic reachability has been projected away.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for causal hedge polynomial delay, uncertain-edge minimal hedge support, and identification probability found no matching causal result. Directed Steiner enumeration and bounded-treewidth transversal enumeration require fully selectable witnesses or an explicit hypergraph, respectively.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash (2025, Definition 6, Algorithm 2, and Lemma 7) because their lazy algorithm already discovers minimal hedges.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their objects are vertex-minimal hedges in one fixed graph and their algorithm discovers only enough of them to solve an intervention hitting-set optimum; uncertain-edge supports can share deterministic paths, collide across hedge cores, and dominate one another globally, and their result supplies no output-sensitive enumeration guarantee.

seed_details.proposal: After the causal compiler emits the minimal-support hypergraph, instantiate standard literal-weighted CNF model counting and project--join dynamic programming to compute total identification probability and its full edge gradient in \(2^{O(\tau)}\) polynomial exact-arithmetic time.
seed_details.anchor_receipt: Read the Introduction, the table-state definition, join recurrence and correctness argument, and the main \(O(4^k k\ell N)\) theorem in the public arXiv PDF. The first changed step replaces clause satisfaction counts by rational Bernoulli weights for negative monotone obstruction clauses.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Translate support avoidance into a negative monotone CNF on uncertain causal edges, then add conditioned evaluations for derivatives and prove bit-length control.
seed_details.destination_search: Exact literal-weighted model counting already supplies the generic computation once the causal compiler has made the obstruction clauses explicit.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from bounded-incidence-treewidth weighted model counting.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds at the algorithmic-novelty level. The item is retained only as a labelled implementation corollary of the causal obstruction compiler, with boundary handling and rational bit complexity stated for reproducibility.

seed_details.proposal: Prove that exact counting of identifiable realizations is \(\#\mathrm{P}\)-complete already when the largest bidirected district has size two, although minimal obstructions have polynomial-delay enumeration there.
seed_details.anchor_receipt: Opened the publisher abstract and theorem summary establishing \(\#\mathrm{P}\)-completeness of source--sink reliability for acyclic directed planar graphs of maximum degree three. The first causal step is a size-two bow gadget, with Shpitser (2023, Proposition 1) converting existence of its original-query hedge into ID failure exactly when the source reaches the sink.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the reachability acceptance event by failure of \(P_x(y)\) through a deterministic bow, invoke Shpitser (2023, Proposition 1) for the original-query hedge equivalence, and keep complementation explicit as a polynomial-time counting reduction.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches found NP-completeness of edge ID but no classification of counting all identifiable realizations, including under district size two.
seed_details.red_team: The result follows automatically from NP-completeness of edge ID.
seed_details.rebuttal: Decision hardness does not imply counting hardness, and the width-two restriction requires the event-preserving original-query hedge equivalence of Shpitser (2023, Proposition 1) rather than the published intervention-design reductions.

seed_details.proposal: Compute identification reliability and factor-parameter sensitivities under locally correlated edge uncertainty in time fixed-parameter tractable in the combined obstruction--factor incidence treewidth.
seed_details.anchor_receipt: Read Assumption 1, Appendix C on perfect correlations, and the concluding statement that general dependence is future work. The first failed independent-edge step is the product normalization used by edge ID.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace independent Bernoulli literals by normalized local factors and prove a junction-tree sum-product recurrence over the combined obstruction--factor incidence graph.
seed_details.destination_search: Goharshady and Mohammadi allow arbitrary distributions within independent edge blocks, and Dudek et al. supply factorized weighted counting; no source found applies them to causal identification reliability.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from factor-graph weighted model counting.
seed_details.rebuttal: The computational part is generic after the causal failure constraints are compiled, leaving less standalone novelty than the enumeration kernel; the seed is therefore not selected for this version.

seed_details.proposal: Partition identifiable ADMG realizations into semantically distinct ordinary-ID functional classes and compute the probability mass of every class without duplicates.
seed_details.anchor_receipt: Read the Introduction, the shortest problematic-path theorem, the IDGraphs recursion, its three-part correctness theorem and proof sketch, and the Discussion. Its uniqueness argument is tied to MPDAG orientations without latent variables.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The MPDAG proof separates two branches by a linear-Gaussian law; with ADMGs, the first new step is a sound-and-complete semantic equivalence criterion for nested district functionals.
seed_details.destination_search: Expression simplification removes redundant sums and factors, but no complete semantic equality test for arbitrary ordinary-ID outputs across ADMG realizations was found.
seed_details.red_team: Guo and Perkovic already give duplicate-free enumeration of distinct causal functionals.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their partition concerns DAGs represented by an MPDAG and total effects; they explicitly note that the strategy does not carry directly to latent-variable graphs. The missing ADMG semantic equivalence theorem is much less feasible than the selected kernel.

seed_details.proposal: For a discrete observational law, characterize the probability distribution of realization-specific sharp causal-bound intervals and the event that their width is at most \(\varepsilon\).
seed_details.anchor_receipt: Read the Introduction, the equivalent polynomial-program construction, the \(\varepsilon\)-sharp branch-and-bound algorithm, and the Future Work section. The first changed step is aggregating graph-specific feasible response-function models under edge-realization weights.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The obstruction event ceases to be Boolean because interval endpoints depend on the observed law; a finite graph-state compression preserving both endpoint optimizers must replace hedge-support avoidance.
seed_details.destination_search: Autobounds treats one fixed graphical model, while PAG-bound work treats an unweighted equivalence class; no exact probability law over sharp intervals was found.
seed_details.red_team: Run Autobounds separately on every realization and sum the weights.
seed_details.rebuttal: That is exponentially many nonconvex programs and gives no graph-native compression, sensitivity theorem, or uniform sharpness certificate. No credible compressed-state theorem emerged, so the seed is deferred.

seed_details.proposal: Compile a shared obstruction basis for a family of intervention--outcome queries and answer joint reliability and query-selection questions without rerunning identification for each query.
seed_details.anchor_receipt: Read the paper's two query-specific optimization formulations and its edge-to-vertex reduction. Both constructions fix one query; no shared-query theorem is given.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Canonicalize recursive ID states across several queries before extracting sparse hedge cores, while preserving query labels under support deletion.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for multi-query uncertain causal identification returned graph-sampling and adjustment robustness tools, not shared minimal hedge-support compilation.
seed_details.red_team: Take the union of the single-query obstruction hypergraphs.
seed_details.rebuttal: A union answers failure of at least one query but does not compress shared recursive certificates or control delay as the number of queries grows; the needed parameterized compression currently lacks evidence.

seed_details.proposal: Characterize inclusion-minimal edge deletions restoring identification as the minimal transversals of the failure-support hypergraph.
seed_details.anchor_receipt: Read Definition 6 and Algorithm 2 on pages 10--12, Lemma 7 on page 12, the minimum-hitting-set equivalence in Lemma 3 and its proof on pages 33--34, and the empirical discussion on pages 20--21 of the final JMLR version. The algorithm discovers only enough vertex hedges to certify an optimal intervention and explicitly avoids full enumeration.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Exchange vertex hedges for uncertain-edge failure supports and dualize the resulting monotone Boolean function.
seed_details.destination_search: The anchor already formulates intervention design as hitting minimal hedges, and standard hypergraph duality supplies the edge-repair statement once the obstruction hypergraph is known.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from the definition of a minimal failure support and hypergraph transversal duality.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds; this is a corollary or consumer interface, not an independent kernel.

seed_details.proposal: Characterize failure for every envelope with \(b\le 2\) by an available bow followed by projected directed reachability, and enumerate all minimal supports as induced paths with polynomial delay and space.
seed_details.anchor_receipt: Read the Introduction, hedge Definition 16, Theorems 17--19, the ID pseudocode, and the Appendix proof that a failed recursive call yields nested rooted C-forests. Shpitser (2023, Proposition 1) supplies the corrected original-query equivalence. The first changed step specializes that certificate under district size two and projects deterministic paths before enumeration.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Use Shpitser (2023, Proposition 1) to prove the if-and-only-if bow--ancestry characterization, then map available bows and uncertain directed edges to explicitly labelled transition vertices and delete forward chords during branching.
seed_details.destination_search: Khachiyan et al. give a special directed path-conjunction delay result and Kobayashi et al. enumerate minimal directed Steiner edge subgraphs, but neither projects deterministic subpaths to uncertain labels.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from polynomial-delay enumeration of directed paths or directed Steiner trees.
seed_details.rebuttal: Ordinary witness enumeration can traverse exponentially many deterministic paths that collapse to one uncertain support; the transition-DAG projection and induced-path invariant are necessary for output-sensitive support enumeration.

adjacent_threads: Shpitser and Pearl (2008), together with Shpitser (2023, Proposition 1), make original-query hedges necessary and sufficient for ordinary-ID failure but do not study uncertain-edge minimal supports.

Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash (2025, Definition 6 and Algorithm 2 on pages 10--12, with Lemma 7) compute a hedge hull and lazily discover enough vertex-minimal hedges for intervention optimization, without enumerating uncertain-edge-minimal original-query failure supports or establishing output-sensitive delay.

Kobayashi, Kurita, and Wasa (2022) obtain linear delay for minimal directed Steiner edge subgraphs; deterministic edges are deletable in their minimality notion, so projected uncertain labels are not covered.

Kenig and Mizrahi (2025) enumerate minimal transversals with fixed-parameter-linear delay from an explicit bounded-incidence-treewidth hypergraph; the causal obstruction hypergraph here is implicit and the parameter is envelope district size.
surviving_candidates.occupied_target_check: No opened source gives coverage, global minimality, duplicate suppression, exhaustion, and \(2^{O(b\log b)}\) delay for minimal uncertain-edge ID-failure supports. The closest enumeration theorems fail at deterministic projection or assume the output hypergraph is already explicit.
surviving_candidates.method_adapted: Adapt ID failure-to-hedge extraction from Shpitser and Pearl, hedge-hull reduction from Akbari et al., and extendable-prefix branching from Steiner and transversal enumeration. The new invariant must assign each uncertain edge to a private root while testing domination by every competing sparse core.

adjacent_threads: Dudek, Phan, and Vardi (2020) express literal-weighted model counting as project--join elimination, supplying the sum--product execution pattern.

Goharshady and Mohammadi (2020) preserve network reliability by shrinking bounded-treewidth networks, but their states encode connectivity of the original network rather than avoidance of causal obstructions.
Akbari et al. (2023) convert independent edge probabilities to additive edge ID weights for selecting one graph, not for summing all identifiable realizations.
Samer and Szeider (2010) prove an incidence-treewidth table recurrence by recording bag-variable assignments and unsatisfied bag clauses.
surviving_candidates.occupied_target_check: Weighted model counting settles the generic computation once \(\mathcal O_{XY}\) is explicit. This item remains only as an implementation corollary of the new compiler; the gradient comes from standard conditioned weighted counts and is not counted as separate novelty.
surviving_candidates.method_adapted: Replace each obstruction by a negative monotone clause, retain assignment and witnessed-zero flags in each incidence bag, and obtain each derivative from two conditioned weighted counts.

adjacent_threads: Provan and Ball (1983) prove exact counting of bipartite vertex covers is \(\#\mathrm{P}\)-complete, providing an all-half-probability source instance.
Akbari et al. (2023) prove NP-completeness of edge ID by reductions through intervention design, which does not classify the realization-counting function.
Shpitser (2023, Proposition 1) gives the corrected equivalence between failure of the original query and an original-query hedge, which is required in both directions of the gadget proof.
Provan (1986) proves source--sink reliability remains \(\#\mathrm{P}\)-complete on acyclic directed planar graphs of maximum degree three.
surviving_candidates.occupied_target_check: No closer paper found counts successful ordinary-ID realizations under bounded bidirected districts. The width-two bow gadget is not present in the reliability or edge ID reductions.
surviving_candidates.method_adapted: Use Shpitser (2023, Proposition 1) to encode source--sink reachability as original-query ID failure through the unique size-two hedge, and reduce exact bipartite independent-set counting to successful realizations by complementation under a polynomial-time counting reduction.

dropped_after_scan: The correlated-factor seed is a direct factor-graph weighted-counting application after obstruction compilation and is less novel than the selected kernel.
The functional-class seed requires a complete semantic equality theory for nested-ID functionals, and the opened MPDAG paper explicitly identifies latent variables as a barrier.
The random-bound-interval seed has no verified finite graph-state compression of realization-specific polynomial programs.
